This child therefore proves the statement itself under the globally unique name rsd_mw_wlm_orient_opNorm_le_one and does not cite the other declaration.

Norms: Covector (Euclid P) n carries the operator norm of continuous alternating maps; MultiVector P n = (Covector (Euclid P) n →L[ℝ] ℝ) carries the operator norm of continuous linear functionals.

1. By the hypothesis IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q, choose a family τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) in ℝ^P with the following properties. τ is orthonormal, and either ξ(α) = α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for every n-covector α, or ξ(α) = −α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for every n-covector α. The spanning property Submodule.span ℝ (range τ) = Q is not used.
2. Fix an n-covector α. Since α is a continuous multilinear map, |α(τ_1, …, τ_n)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_{i=1}^n ‖τ_i‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm). Orthonormality gives ‖τ_i‖ = 1 for every i (the first component of Orthonormal), so the product equals 1; for n = 0 it is the empty product 1. Hence |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖.
3. In either sign case of step 1, |ξ(α)| = |±α(τ)| = |α(τ)| ≤ 1·‖α‖.
4. Step 3 holds for every n-covector α, and 1 ≥ 0. By the defining property of the operator norm of the continuous linear functional ξ (ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound), ‖ξ‖ ≤ 1. ∎
